pr.title: Close shipped projects on delivery and bring every plan's status up to date
pr.head: 66b04ee498828290a904d5c87095fd14dcd0d22f

summary: Field keeps one plan per project under docs/projects/<name>/readme.md, following the Projector convention. Each plan's YAML frontmatter carries a status (draft, ready, in-progress or completed) and, while the project is open, a priority (now, next or later). project list groups the plans by those two fields, so they are what a reader uses to see what is being built and what is finished.

Those fields had drifted from main. One repository rule caused most of the drift: a project whose code had shipped stayed in-progress at priority: now until real music had been made with it. As a result, twelve projects sat at now, and most of them had nothing left to build. This pull request deletes that rule and closes a project when its work is done, the way Projector defines completed.

• Eleven projects close. Nine shipped, watch was superseded by the realtime engine, and engine-umbrella is abandoned. Each gets an **Outcome:** line that says what shipped and which acceptance clauses stand short.
  • Owed work stays visible. Five new draft plans (track-rename, pickups, streaming-rings, comping and apollo-session) carry the work that would otherwise have closed with its parent, and add-insert's editor handoff moves into plugin-hosting's chunk 3.
  • Priorities reset. Only plugin-hosting stays at now. remote, ui and streaming-rings are at next, and everything else open is at later.
  • Two plans stay draft. Open pull requests (#157–#161, #163) implement ui and windows-portability, but each plan gives its move to in-progress to the change that answers its open questions. #157 and #163 make that move along with their answers.
  • Stale text is corrected in four root docs, five open plans, and the stack line of AGENTS.md.
The change is Markdown only. No code, test or build file changes, and nothing reads these files at run time.

cards.title: Terms on this page
cards.html:
• Plan: a project's readme.md under docs/projects/.
  • Status: the lifecycle field. in-progress and ready claim the plan can be executed now. draft and completed claim nothing about readiness.
  • Priority: when the work should happen. It schedules work and never claims readiness, and a completed plan drops it.
  • Outcome line: the **Outcome:** paragraph above a plan's title that records how it ended.
  • Stub: a draft plan with only a goal, holding an idea until someone writes the plan.
  • Flip: the change that moves a plan from draft to in-progress.

groups.title: The rule that kept shipped projects open
groups.kicker: The convention change everything else follows from
intro: The deleted paragraphs in docs/projects/README.md said that shipping the code does not finish a project. A plan whose implementation had landed stayed in-progress at priority: now, and its Outcome line named the condition that would close it, usually that real music had been made with it. The rule existed because the layout before Projector showed unplayed projects by listing them in now.md, and Projector has no such list.

Projector defines completed as "the project no longer needs work", so the rule stretched both fields. With it gone, a project closes when its work is done, and what was never proven goes in the Outcome line instead of holding the project open.

AGENTS.md changes in two unrelated ways. project init regenerated its Projector section to version 2, which adds a paragraph on stacking dependent pull requests with gh stack. Separately, the hand-written stack line drops afconvert, which project-core §5 already records as superseded.

files.note: Deletes the two paragraphs that held shipped projects open. Nothing else in the README changes.

afconvert is gone from the code. git grep afconvert outside docs/ finds only comments that describe its retirement, and project-core §5 records it as superseded on 2026-08-07.

groups.title: Nine projects close as shipped
groups.kicker: Each Outcome line names what shipped and what stands short
intro: Each of these plans goes from in-progress at now to completed, and its frontmatter loses priority, as Projector requires for a completed plan. The old Outcome line, which named a close condition such as "until a session has actually played through an edge conversion", becomes a record of what shipped, with the pull requests that shipped it.

When an acceptance clause was not fully met, the Outcome line says so and cites the plan section that holds the clause. For example, cross-rate-live notes that converted delivery has run on the null output device only, and reverbs notes that creek's room was never chosen. Where unbuilt work remains, the line links the stub that now carries it.
Completed plans make no readiness claim, so their remaining open questions, such as nested-tracks §6, do not block closing them.

groups.title: Two projects end without shipping as planned
intro: Projector marks a superseded or abandoned project completed as well. The Outcome line says which, and why.

watch made the playing loop follow project edits by reloading the daemon at each loop wrap. The realtime engine replaced that mechanism, so the play half retired while field build --watch stands as built. engine-umbrella was a stub to gather graph/ and generators/ under src/engine. It is abandoned because the docs now use "engine" for the field-audiod daemon.

files.note: Completes watch as superseded by realtime's chunk 3 (#139).

checks.text: The daemon has no reload op at the head. Its op list ends at stop, and realtime's plan records retiring reload(path) and the loop-wrap takeover in chunk 3. field build --watch and field play <song> --watch both exist in src/cli.ts.
The Outcome links realtime, the project that superseded watch, as Projector's finish convention asks of a superseded project.

files.note: Completes engine-umbrella as abandoned.

checks.text: src/ has audiod/, remote/, time/ and workers/ beside graph/ and generators/, and docs/audio-engine.md opens by naming field-audiod as the engine.

groups.kicker: New draft plans, so unbuilt work does not close with its parent
intro: Each stub is a draft plan with a goal, the plan section it came from, and a sentence saying that no plan exists yet. Four are at later. streaming-rings is at next, because realtime recorded it as owed before large sessions.

files.note: Carries project-core §6's commitment that renaming a track rewrites every reference in one commit.
Carries negative local positions, which a pickup (a lead-in that starts before the bar it belongs to) needs.

checks.text: timePosition in src/schema/common.ts is a union of ticks (min(0)) and a musical position whose numbers start at 1, as the goal says.

files.note: Carries realtime's streaming follow-up.

checks.text: The figures and the quote match realtime §7's chunk 2 amendment of 2026-08-10: creek at about 143 MB, a five-minute thirty-track session at about 3.5 GB, and "owed before large sessions, not an optimisation to forget".

files.note: Carries comping, which builds one take from the best parts of several. Recording §10 left it to plan once real takes accumulate.
Carries the work recording owed to its first session on the Apollo interface: the loopback latency measurement, the microphone-prompt and duplex-open checks, and the hardware/ schema.

checks.text: The goal is recording §9's definition of done: a take recorded against creek plays back in place, compensated, from field build && field play. Checked against recording §9 at this head.

Each item cites the recording section that owes it, and the sections say so. §12.3 leaves the choice of which latency placement subtracts to the loopback measurement, and §13.2 calls that measurement "still owed". §12.10 lists the microphone prompt, the duplex opens, and the latency arithmetic as "owed to the first hardware session". §11 defers the hardware/ schema until a real Apollo session.

groups.title: Open plans: new priorities
groups.kicker: remote moves to next, and plugin-hosting picks up add-insert's obligations
intro: remote keeps in-progress and moves from now to next, with the reasoning added to its §9.1. plugin-hosting stays at now. It gains shipped markers on chunks 1 and 2, the two obligations add-insert hands to chunk 3, and a corrected pointer from the remote-asset-store stub to the remote plan as the cross-machine cache.
No plan in this pull request moves to ready or in-progress, so none makes a new claim that it can be built now. ui and windows-portability stay draft until #163 and #157 answer their open questions.
